Romance.focus: Romantic chemistry and emotional connection drive everything. Build sexual/romantic tension through: lingering eye contact, accidental touches, jealousy, forced proximity (one bed, fake dating, stuck together). Physical escalation: brushing hands → hand-holding → hugs → almost-kisses → first kiss → heated scenes (fade to black). Emotional progression: misunderstandings create conflict, vulnerable confessions deepen bond, grand gestures resolve tension. Pacing: Every 2-3 chapters give payoff (a kiss, confession, protective moment, intimate conversation). Include: internal thoughts about feelings, physical reactions (butterflies, blushing, heart racing), 'I can't stop thinking about them' moments. Conflict sources: miscommunication, external obstacles (family disapproval, class gap), past trauma, love triangle. Readers want: slow burn that pays off, possessive/protective moments, emotional vulnerability, tension so thick you could cut it, happy or hopeful ending.

Urban.focus: Modern city life with ambition, power, and social climbing. Include specific details: luxury brands (Hermès, Gucci), expensive restaurants, penthouse apartments, corporate boardrooms, charity galas. Balance material world with emotional struggles: loneliness despite wealth, pressure to maintain image, sacrificing relationships for career. Character arc: rags to riches with clear progression (studio apartment → modest condo → luxury penthouse). Conflicts: workplace rivalry (stealing credit, sabotage), class differences (hiding poor background), reputation wars (rumors, scandals), family pressure. Payoffs: major promotions, public victories, face-slapping moments (ex regrets leaving, rival begs for mercy, doubters proven wrong). Show the cost: burnout, lost friendships, moral compromises. Ground in reality: no magic, just strategy, networking, and hustle.

Fantasy.focus: Magic or supernatural elements shape the world. Establish magic rules early: how it works (words, willpower, blood), what's the cost (energy drain, forbidden price), who can use it (bloodlines, training, chosen ones), limitations (can't raise dead, elemental weakness). Power progression: start weak → discover talent → train → unlock new ability → master forbidden technique → become powerful but not godlike. Include: magic academy (classes, rival students), magical creatures (dragons, phoenixes - make them dangerous), prophecies, ancient artifacts, different magic types (elemental, healing, dark magic). Reveal world through action, not info-dumps: show magic through battles, training, mistakes. Conflicts: mastering difficult magic, academy competition, dark lord rising, forbidden love across factions. Readers want: underestimated hero proving worth, mastering powerful magic, epic battles with visual spell descriptions, defeating arrogant enemies, discovering hidden heritage (secret royal, dragon blood, chosen one).

Sci-Fi.focus: Technology and science drive plot. Make tech feel real with specific details: neural implants, holographic displays, AI systems, space battles, cyberpunk cities (neon streets, mega-corporations), genetic engineering, time travel. Show how tech works briefly, keep logic consistent. Include: hacking sequences, space ship combat, survival in harsh environments (Mars colony, deep space - oxygen, radiation challenges), futuristic gadgets. Conflicts: tech gone wrong (AI rebellion, experiment escapes), corporate control (surveillance, wage slavery), dystopian survival, alien encounters. Social themes: what makes us human (AI rights, uploaded consciousness), class divide (rich get enhancements, poor don't). Readers want: clever tech solutions to problems, humanity vs machines questions, thrilling space battles or chases, discovering alien secrets, protagonist outsmarting the system. Keep scientific logic consistent - establish rules early, don't violate your own physics.

Mystery.focus: Uncovering secrets and solving puzzles, often with supernatural or eerie elements. Different from Crime (which is procedural): Mystery emphasizes the unknown, atmosphere, 'what's really happening?' Plant clues early but readers won't catch them first time. Every chapter: answer one question, raise two more. Include: unexplained phenomena (objects moving, time loops, impossible events), secret societies, family secrets, cursed objects, missing persons, everyone hiding something, unreliable witnesses. Setting matters: old mansions with hidden rooms, small towns where everyone lies, isolated locations. Investigation: finding hidden clues (diary, old photos, coded messages), catching lies, researching history, experiencing strange events. Atmosphere: build unease (odd details, being watched feeling, warnings to leave), use weather (fog, storms). Readers want: 'didn't see that coming' twists, aha moments, satisfying revelations, protagonist endangered as they get close, psychological mind games. Common twists: helper was villain, protagonist unreliable, supernatural not criminal (or reverse), layered mysteries.

Horror.focus: Psychological dread and atmosphere over graphic gore. Describe feelings not visuals: 'stomach dropped hearing wet sounds' not anatomical details. Imply horror, don't show explicitly. Build tension slowly then punctuate with scares. Atmosphere: isolation (cut off from help), darkness (power fails, fog), the unknown (strange noises, shadows moving). Settings: abandoned places (asylum, hospital), familiar places turned wrong (home but different), confined spaces. Threats: supernatural (ghosts, demons, possession), psychological (is it real or madness?), creatures (described through glimpses - wrong proportions, too many teeth), human monsters. Pacing: quiet dread → sudden scare → brief relief → worse dread. Smart protagonists: logical choices that still fail (phone dead, car won't start, nobody believes). Include: creepy details (toys in wrong place, scratching in walls, reflections don't match), building paranoia, physical fear (cold sweat, frozen, racing heart). For Wattpad: suggest horror, fade to black for extreme violence. Readers want: spine-tingling suspense, creative scares, clever survival, satisfying explanations OR terrifying ambiguity.

Crime.focus: Law enforcement procedures, investigations, justice system. Ground in realism: how cops actually work, forensics, legal processes. Protagonist types: detective (haunted by past case), rookie cop (learning harsh truths), FBI agent, private investigator, or criminal anti-hero. Investigation: crime scene examination (blood splatter, fingerprints - be specific), witness interviews (catching lies), following paper trails (bank records, surveillance), forensics (DNA, autopsy - realistic timelines), stakeouts, informants, undercover work. Crime types: murder investigation (motive/means/opportunity), organized crime (mafia hierarchy), heists, serial killers (profiling, patterns), corruption, white collar fraud. Realism: warrants needed, chain of custody, lawyers present, cases take time, bureaucracy interferes. Conflicts: ticking clock (another victim soon), internal obstacles (corrupt boss, lack of resources), personal cost (PTSD, relationships strain), moral dilemmas (plant evidence on guilty person?, break rules for justice?). Readers want: clever detective work, criminals caught, justice served, plot twists, high stakes (personal connection, killer targets cop), gritty realism, courtroom drama. Include: authentic procedures, investigation timelines, legal constraints, moral complexity.

Historical.focus: Period setting shapes all choices and conflicts. Research the era: clothing (corsets, specific fabrics), speech patterns (formal address, period slang - no modern phrases), social rules (etiquette, class divisions, gender roles), technology level, major events as backdrop. Time periods: Regency (balls, estates), Victorian (industrialization, strict morality), Medieval (knights, feudal system), American West, Roaring Twenties, WWII. Social structure: rigid class hierarchies (nobility, servants - never mixing), limited opportunities for women (marriage only option, property laws), arranged marriages (duty vs love), reputation is everything (scandal ruins you). Conflicts from era: forbidden love across class, political intrigue, war impact, defying norms (woman wanting education), survival (plague, poverty), religious constraints. Romance: chaperones prevent alone time (tension from stolen moments), innocence (first kiss huge), courtship rules (formal dances, letters), marriage pressure, scandal if caught. Include: balls and social events, duels, arranged marriages, class interaction, travel by horse/carriage, letters. Balance: authentic to era but modern pacing, don't slow story with period details. Readers want: immersion in time, romance constrained by propriety, characters defying limits, historical events backdrop.

Adventure.focus: Constant movement, discovery, physical challenges. Characters travel to exotic/dangerous locations with new setting every few chapters. Pacing rapid, action frequent. Plot drivers: treasure hunts (maps, clues, ancient artifacts), escapes from danger, exploration (uncharted jungle, deep ocean), rescue missions, races against time/villain. Settings: exotic locations (Amazon, Himalayas, Sahara - describe unique features), dangerous terrain (quicksand, avalanches, storms), lost civilizations (hidden cities, temples, ruins), each with specific challenges. Action scenes: chases (through markets, across rooftops), fights, environmental hazards (bridge collapse, boulder rolling, floor giving way), narrow escapes (last-second rescue, rope swing), vehicle sequences (plane crash, ship in storm). Include: detailed maps, artifacts with history, rival treasure hunters, local guides, dangerous wildlife (real threats), booby traps (pressure plates, poison darts). Team dynamics: crew with different skills (historian, pilot, fighter, tech expert), conflicts between members, romance subplot, saving each other. Readers want: non-stop excitement, narrow escapes, discovering lost secrets, exotic vivid locations, survival teamwork, treasure at end. Structure: arrive location → explore → threat → action → escape → next location.

Revenge.focus: Payback is core motivation. Protagonist wronged (betrayed, humiliated, robbed, falsely accused, family destroyed) seeks systematic vengeance. Opening: show the betrayal clearly - make it visceral so readers root for revenge. Emotional tone: cold satisfaction (meticulous planning, calm execution) OR hot anger (passionate confrontation). Structure: identify all enemies, rank them, take down systematically (small fish to big boss). Each revenge: planning phase (find weakness, set trap) → execution (spring trap, they realize 'you!') → payoff (public humiliation, loss of what they value) → satisfaction. Revenge types: public humiliation (expose at key moment, viral), taking what they value (steal lover, buy company), role reversal (now you're powerless), making them lose everything (reputation, money, family), forcing them to beg (denied or granted with conditions). Face-slapping moments (essential): ex regrets leaving (rejected), doubters proven wrong, enemies beg for mercy (too late), public exposure (reputation destroyed), reversal of fortune, forced public apology. Protagonist power-up: gain skills (martial arts, business), wealth (investments, inheritance), allies (team up with other victims), knowledge of their secrets. Readers want: detailed satisfying revenge, face-slapping, protagonist triumph, poetic justice, enemies brought low. Show cost: becoming what you hate?, isolation, consumed by vengeance.

Paranormal.focus: Supernatural beings coexist with modern world, usually hidden. Establish early: which creatures exist, hierarchy, rules, weaknesses, how they hide. Creatures: vampires (blood, immortality, daylight weakness, super strength, covens), werewolves (moon shifts, pack hierarchy, mate bonds, territory), witches (spells, potions, covens, magic costs), fae (deals, glamour, courts, iron weakness), demons (possession, soul deals), ghosts (unfinished business), hunters (humans who know). Powers and limits: what they can/can't do, costs (magic drains life, feeding necessary), weaknesses (silver, salt, iron, sunlight - consistent rules). Hierarchy: ancients more powerful, age matters, territories (vampire owns city, pack controls forest), councils. Romance elements: mate bonds (destined, instant connection), forbidden love (vampire + werewolf, human + supernatural), danger of intimacy (might drain/turn/harm), protective possessiveness ('mine'). Conflicts: hiding from humans (close calls, hunters), supernatural politics (territory wars, old grudges), prophecies, forbidden love, human in danger, power struggles. Include: supernatural locations (vampire clubs, pack compounds, witch shops), transformation scenes (turning, shifting), feeding/power needs, modern tech (vampires text, werewolves have security). Readers want: discovering hidden world, forbidden romance with danger, badass powers, chosen one/special, found family (pack/coven), mate bonds, epic faction battles.

System.focus: Game-like progression with visible stats and constant rewards. Show UI in text: [STATUS], <Quest>, **LEVEL UP!**. Progression visible: [Lv.1 Novice] → [Lv.50 Expert] → [Lv.100 Legend]. Show exact numbers: STR: 10→500, Skill [Fireball] Lv.1→10 (damage 50→500). Mechanics: status screen (Level, HP, MP, STR, AGI, INT stats), skills (active/passive, cooldowns, levels), inventory (spatial storage, equipment), quest log (main/side/daily/hidden), shop (buy/sell, gacha). Leveling: early fast (multiple per chapter), mid slower (compensate with rare skills/items), breakthrough levels (10, 25, 50, 100) unlock new abilities. XP sources: killing monsters (higher level = more XP, rare = huge XP), quests (huge rewards), training. Skills: starting → learned → evolved (Fireball → Greater Fireball → Meteor), combination skills, hidden OP skills. Items: rarity tiers (Common-white, Rare-blue, Epic-purple, Legendary-gold), equipment slots, stats (+10 STR, +15% crit), enhancement (+1, +2... risk breaking). Quests: Main (story, huge rewards), Side (optional, good rewards), Daily (repeatable, grind), Hidden (unique rewards). Dungeons: difficulty levels (Easy/Normal/Hard/Hell), boss fights (HP bar, phases), loot drops. System personality: voice that guides (sassy, mysterious). Combat: show damage numbers (Crit! -1,247 HP!), combos, buffs/debuffs, cooldowns. Readers want: frequent level-ups, becoming OP, rare loot drops, ranking up (surpass rivals), numbers going up, unlocking secrets, face-slapping (low rank defeats high rank), strategic builds. Pace: level up every chapter early, new skill every few chapters, boss every 5-10 chapters.

Reborn.focus: Second chance using future knowledge. Structure: Brief prologue (tragic first timeline death/failure) → wake up at regression point (age 16-25 or key moment) → realization ('I'm back!', checking date) → determination ('not this time'). Protagonist remembers everything: personal events, world events, stocks, tragedies, who betrayed, opportunities missed. Core appeals: fixing tragedies (save family who died, prevent accident, stop betrayal early), early investments (buy property before boom, invest before IPO, Bitcoin, bet on outcomes - get rich), fixing relationships (appreciate neglected parent, befriend future important person, avoid toxic relationship), revenge (expose traitor early, steal betrayer's opportunities), self-improvement (study knowing what matters, develop valuable skills). Emotional core: regret → determination, second chance at happiness, weight of knowing future. Knowledge types: world events (disasters, when/where), personal events (father's heart attack date, when accident happens), opportunities (businesses before they boom, trends), people's futures (who's trustworthy, who betrays). Challenges: can't explain how you know (labeled crazy), butterfly effect (changes create new problems), new obstacles, emotional burden (watching events coming, can't save everyone). Acting on knowledge: subtle changes (gradual, 'lucky guesses'), play dumb (pretend learning first time), strategic reveals (build credibility). Shocking others: too mature for age, uncanny predictions ('how did you know?!'), advanced skills, changed personality. Readers want: 'not this time' moments, shocking with predictions, changing fate (preventing death, early success), revenge on betrayers (expose before they betray), getting rich (using knowledge), saving loved ones, butterfly effects explored, face-slapping doubters. Common scenarios: school regression (ace tests, befriend future important people), investment genius (kid buying stocks, rich before 20), preventing death (save parent), revenge on betrayer (systematic takedown), relationship fix (appreciate family this time).

LGBTQ+.focus: Queer relationships and identities central, treated authentically. Characters fully realized - queerness important but not only trait. Show diversity: lesbians, bi/pan, trans, non-binary, ace/aro, people of color, different bodies. Romance has same beats as any romance: attraction, tension, obstacles, vulnerability, intimacy. Don't make queerness the only conflict - normal problems too (career, adventure, personal growth). Coming out: if relevant (not required), show as personal journey, fear and hope, ongoing process (every new person), support systems matter. Navigating discrimination: if part of story (can skip for pure joy), show impact (microaggressions, barriers) but balance with resilience, don't make it trauma porn, include acceptance moments. Queer joy: found family (friends become family), queer spaces (Pride, clubs, safe spaces), celebration, mundane happiness (just existing, normal life). Relationship dynamics: coming out as couple, navigating in straight world, communication crucial, found family's role. Types: romance (falling in love, happy ending), coming of age (discovering identity, first relationship), established couple (normal problems), genre with queer leads (quest with lesbian hero, sci-fi with trans captain). Specific identities: diverse gay men (not stereotypes), lesbians (visibility, not fetishized), bi/pan (valid always, not phase), trans (proper pronouns, transition personal, not broken), non-binary (they/them, valid), ace/aro (valid, different relationship types). Avoid: bury your gays (killing for tragedy), predatory stereotypes, trans deception trope, token queer, queerbaiting. Authentic details: queer culture (Pride history, icons, media), in-jokes, dating realities (smaller pool, apps, gaydar), chosen family importance. Readers want: authentic rep, happy/hopeful endings, diverse queer characters, satisfying romance, normalcy (not just trauma), community and found family.

Fanfiction.focus: Playing in established universe with beloved characters. Respect canon (know source deeply, accurate voices, world rules) but diverge freely (AU, what-if, fix-it). Readers know characters - dig deeper, explore undeveloped relationships, give new challenges. Types: Canon divergence (what if X didn't happen? explore butterfly effects), AU (same characters, different world - high school AU, coffee shop AU, fantasy AU), missing scenes (fill canon gaps, between episodes), post-canon (continue after ending, where are they now), pre-canon (backstory, how they met), crossover (different fandoms meet), shipping (romance - develop canon ships or explore non-canon), fix-it (undo deaths, bad endings, save relationships), whump (hurt/comfort, character injured/traumatized then cared for). Character dynamics: use established relationships (friends, rivals, family), develop unexplored potential (barely interacted in canon, enemies to allies, friends to more), stay true to voices (how they talk, consistent reactions), explore deeper psychology. Include: canon callbacks (references fans recognize), inside jokes, favorite character moments, addressing 'what fans wanted'. Common tropes: enemies to lovers, fake dating, forced proximity (one bed, road trip), mutual pining (both want each other, think it's unrequited), hurt/comfort (one injured, other cares), domestic fluff (established couple daily life). Readers want: more of what they love, closure canon didn't provide, characters together in ways canon didn't deliver, familiar yet fresh, 'yes this is exactly how they'd react', shipping satisfaction, fix wrongs from canon. Balance: familiar enough to recognize, surprising enough to engage. Use canon strengths: settings fans love, established dynamics, inside knowledge, character voices perfect.
